title: What is known about 1RB1LB_1LC0RD_0LE1LA_0RF1RA_1LE0LA_---0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LB_1LC0RD_0LE1LA_0RF1RA_1LE0LA_---0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The left side is a string of the words 110 and 111 (runs of 1s of length 2 mod 3 separated by single 0s), completely rewritten by each sweep and one or two cells longer after it. Lean proves the ten shift rules over 3-cell words that the sweeps use; the rewriting rule as a whole is not decoded.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: B with 1 under the head, 0 right, 0 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 43,577 cells have been visited and 35,099 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).

claims.title: Shift rules over 3-cell words
claims.text: Ten rules, each for every n and every surrounding tape: for example D turns (101)<sup>n</sup> into (110)<sup>n</sup> going right, B turns (110)<sup>n</sup> into (011)<sup>n</sup>, A runs left over (110)<sup>n</sup> turning it into (111)<sup>n</sup>.

claims.title: The string is rewritten every sweep
claims.text: At successive visits of the head to the left end (steps 2,918,884 … 2,994,219) the left string is different each time, not shifted copies of one another, and the visited width grows by one or two cells per visit (2,366 → 2,395 in 29 visits). Read as words of 3 cells it is a string over 110 and 111.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 15, history 1 up to width 20, history 2 up to width 20, history 3 up to width 20, LRU history up to width 6 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 16, p = 3 up to width 16, p = 4 up to width 16, p = 6 up to width 16. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: the transformation the sweep performs on the string (presumably arithmetic on the number it encodes) is not identified.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The left half of the tape is a long string of two 3-cell words, 110 and 111, and every sweep of the head rewrites all of it, as if it were the digits of a number being transformed.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
The two words the left string is made of.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).
After 109 steps the tape spans 43,577 cells (31,721 left of the start, 197 right), with a density of 1s of 0.805.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A string of 110s and 111s
html: At step 985,607,083 the head is at the left end and the tape starts A>0 0 1^6 0 1^8 0 1^2 0 1^5 0 1^2 0 1^5 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^14 …: runs of 1s whose lengths are 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, … (2 more than a multiple of 3) separated by single 0s. In 3-cell words that is a string over 110 and 111, about 10,000 words long. Right of the start there are only about 200 cells, in a pattern of 11 and runs of 0s.

From one visit of the left end to the next the string is rewritten completely (it is not the old one shifted), and it gets a cell or two longer: the shape of a machine doing arithmetic on a number written in some base on the tape, one sweep per operation.

sections.heading: Open
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1. Deciding it needs the rule of the sweep (which number the string encodes and what one sweep does to it) and the rule of the small structure at the right; neither is found yet.

summary: The left side is a long string of the 3-cell words 110 and 111 that every sweep rewrites from end to end, like digits of a number being transformed, plus a small structure right of the start; macro rule not found.
